You've only seen 40% of Machu Picchu. ⛰️ Watch the Inca build it in 26 seconds. ⏱️

They cleared a ridge 2,430 m up between two peaks and quarried the granite right there. Under every terrace: big rocks first, then gravel, then sand, then topsoil, so the heavy rain drains away instead of washing the city off the mountain. About 700 terraces, stone walls fitted without mortar, a Temple of the Sun and around 200 buildings.

The twist: engineer Kenneth Wright estimated about 60% of the work is underground, in foundations and drainage you never see.

Would you have carried stone up here? Yes or no 👇

Next: Sydney Opera House. Follow so you don't miss it.

yt_title: How Machu Picchu Was Built: 60% Is Hidden Underground #shorts
yt_description:
Built c. 1450 on a saddle 2,430 m up between Machu Picchu and Huayna Picchu: the ridge cleared, granite quarried on site, terraces layered with rock, gravel, sand and topsoil for drainage (~700 terraces, ~130 drainage holes), dry-stone walls fitted without mortar, the Temple of the Sun and ~200 structures. Engineer Kenneth Wright estimated about 60% of the construction is underground.

Sources: https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/article/wright-inca-engineering/ · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machu_Picchu
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
